[b]Committee on Eastern Elseyr[/b]

Socialist International would observe events as they were transpiring in the Peoples Union of Thýven and the Vespurian Empire. It was readily apparent to those in the International's Presidium that the conservative orders of both states had been severely shaken by geopolitical events, but the extent to which they were fragile enough to succumb to the people's struggle was another question entirely. 

For the Vespurian Empire, things remain stable for now, and despite relentless Sanguinian interference in Vespurian politics, it seems that their transition into communism may have to be done peacefully. The people remain well-fed, government services remain functional, and there seems to be a powerful loyalty to the status quo, especially in light of the recent White Tree Crisis. For this, the Socialist International would prioritize continued radicalization of local political machines and student organizations so that victory in the Vespurias could be obtained through a parliamentarian approach.

No major Vespurian communist figures would be listed yet, and as far as the Socialist International is concerned, the Almstedt siblings remain the only competent central leaders of the revolution there.

The case of the Peoples Union of Thýven (or simply Thyven) was another case entirely. This state had been the site of extreme domestic chaos for some time now, constantly switching between major geopolitical decisions ever since the collapse of the Elseyro-Vespurian Empire. Because of this, the people's loyalty to state institutions is dubious at best, and the government itself struggles on establishing a clear identity for the Thrømm nation. It is for this reason that we have strong belief in that state's ability to fall into communism.

However, events in Thyven have proceeded far faster than we could've foreseen. We had initially sought to instigate the communist revolution in Vespurias first, where Socialist International's agents are most powerful, and to then use events there as a springboard for the chaos in Thyven. However, it is now clear to us that a revision of these operations must be undertaken.

Thyven will be the first to fall into communism, and so it is the duty of the Socialist International to ensure that the revolution is done well, that it does not betray the fundamental princples of socialism, and that the revolution will be able to eradicate all counterrevolutionary movements that will inevitably spring up to restore the institutions of the old. For these, several parameters must be taken into account:

[list]

1. The Thrømm have had very little contact with communism until recently, which limits their capacity to obey Citharo's political line without direct support. 

2. The International has no viable means to insert its agents into Thyven. as the entirety of our international apparatuses are human, thereby limiting our domestic impact.

3. Piter Drømm, one of the main persons of interest in Thyven's case, is a member of the old guard. His political position is tenuous and his ideology potentially revisionist. Furthermore, his premiership over Thyven has been wrought with unusual geopolitical actions against Daesun and the EDU, making him an impractical wild card.

4. No relevant persons of interest come close to Drømm's relevance.

5. Thyven's economy is hostile to imports, and several of its key industries are fiercely nationalistic. The ability of the state to cooperate with Socialist International's economic model is suspect.

6. The state is currently engaged in the Tallislandic Civil War, an intraimperialist conflict between fascists and revisionists. The state's entry into the Socialist International risks forcing the organization to join in the conflict for a party fundamentally incompatible with our ideological line.

7. THEP, Thyven's primarily political alliance, is constituted by centrists and socialist revisionists. Some of THEP's powers are known to consort with imperialists and fascists on the far-right. The instigation of a communist revolution in Thyven risks fragmenting their geopolitical priorities.

8. Thyven itself is not a unified political entity but a neo-feudal collection of states, with North Thyven, Knygta, and Deyn effectively capable of determining their own fate. Communism requires centralization, which may conflict with Thyven's national character.

[/list]

in the simplest terms possible, Thyven's politics risk drawing the Socialist International into several hidden pathways that it was, at the moment, ill-equipped and ill-prepared to achieve. It was not as simple as waging a triumphant revolution to depose the Ancien Regime and then inculcate the resulting state towards the Citharo line. In the Presidium's mind, it was fundamentally impractical to impose a revolutionary vanguard and lead a proletarian revolution, when Thyven has yet to finish the first stage, that is, the bourgeois revolution to abolish all traces of feudalism from its society.

And so, a Committee on Eastern Elseyr would be developed by the Presidium of the Socialist International, to be composed primarily of Sanguinian and Vespurian agents, whose task it was to carefully observe the Drømm premiership and fund any secret mass organizations looking to liberate Thyven from its neo-feudalist practices. Furthermore, the Presidium would conclude that victory in Thyven will require the International to weaken the leverage of the People's Republican Army, a revisionist entity seeking the independence of Knygta and Deyn at the cost of fragmenting the people's revolution.

Argo Lo Pilato, Pio Graci, Menelao Impastato, Immacolata Terrasi, Caio Graci, and Cirino Sferrazza would be assembled to guide this Committee and outline what must be done for the triumph of the Thyvenian Revolution. In a series of opinion pieces, various courses of action would be considered:

[list]

[u]Lo Pilato[/u]: [i]"Thyven still has no organized political movement capable of pursuing the Citharo line. Instead, it is a confused organization of left tendencies only unified under the person of Mr. Drømm. There is no revolutionary future in which the cult of personality supplants the party. Before any revolutionary struggle can be instigated, we must first put total pressure on the Drømm ministry to organize a communist party, with a politburo and central committee, which may then establish a parallel power to Thyven's imperialist political institutions."[/i]

[u]P. Graci[/u]: [i]"An interesting thing to point out is Thyven's unusual religious character, which gravitates seemingly randomly between Christianity on one side and Thrømm paganism on the other. It is majority Orthodox, but vestiges of the old ways that permeate throughout its national character. A successful revolution can therefore integrate Christian social teaching in doxa and pagan communitarian practices in praxis to build a communist party that deviates, but does not revise socialism, and that is relevant to Thyven's domestic politics."[/i]

[u]Impastato[/u]:[i] "A hypothetical communist party for Thyven will require a politburo appointed by the Socialist International, same as with the revolutions in Astanir and Gythena. Drømm's politics remain too moderate for our liking, and as such we must ensure that he is surrounded by theoreticians and workers who are more malleable and acceptable to the cause of socialism."[/i]

[u]Terrasi[/u]: [i]"The Thrømm economy is fiercely patriotic; you never see any foreign-made cars traversing through the nation's mountain roads and cities. However, as the nation continues to enter into conflict with the EDU and with Daesun, this protectionist system has been challenged by stock fluctuations, which have since been exacerbated by the state's formal intervention in the Tallislandic Civil War. Whatever revolution is established in Thyven should promote internationalism and global cooperation with Socialist International's common market. Qunarco, Somare, Miwu, and Almstedt are all eager to begin doing business in Thyven, but unless the nation is able and willing to make this happen, problems may abound."[/i]

[u]C. Graci[/u]: [i]"Thrømm naval power is untested and often misused as a bargaining chip against EDU forces. A big stick, constantly thrown, becomes smaller with each misuse until it becomes a geopolitical quagmire. A new communist government should be educated in the strategy implemented by QASICOCEAN during its operations in the Astaniran Civil War so as to maximize its overall benefits to the state."[/i]

[u]Sferrazza[/u]: [i]"Thrømm institutions follow a top-down basis of political power, in which authority is exerted by Elseyran liberal institutions trickling down to the populace who benefit from the system. This creates a nation state that is socially centralized but institutionally decentralized, with authority placed in the hands of a network of neo-feudal domains that lord over a bound populace. The revolution in Thyven must be opposite: Socially decentralized through a network of people's soviets, but institutionally centralized through a supreme political organ."[/i]

[/list]

Simply put, the People's Union of Thyven needed extensive reform. The opinions of this Committee would be organized according to a memo, which would be secretly distributed both online and physically to the constituents

It was proceeding down a leftward path, but the process itself was done within the framework imposed by the nation's own liberal democratic model. For there to be a true revolution, done in obedience to the Citharo line, a network of communes or soviets must be organized by the workers to act in parallel to the liberal democratic government, which should sequentially and gradually coopt the functions of the state until it itself becomes the state.

A communist party needed to be formed, which will lead in the creation of these communes so that the destruction of the state will not lead to chaos and anarchy but a transition to a people's democratic state. This party had to be organized according first to a central committee of local representatives, then a political bureau (politburo) of the highest party elites which was to remain in contact with the Socialist International at all times. The intended composition of this hypothetical politburo remains speculative as the Socialist International begins its work determining agents that are friendly to the interests of the Citharo Line.

Economically, the People's Union had prematurely nationalized its industries to obey left opportunist pressures, but the timing is not yet, for this nationalization had been committed for the benefit of civil bureaucrats rather than communist revolutionaries. Thus, the state risks collapsing into a deformity of the proletarian dictatorship. Under Terrasi's recommendation, Thyven should provisionally suspend its talks of mass nationalization of the key industries and first negotiate trade agreements with the member states of the Socialist International, and to only then, upon the development of advanced capitalism, consider economic nationalization of socially significant sectors to aid its transition to a socialist market economy.

The International also recommended taking control of Thyven's geopolitical orientation to restrain its recent spate of misadventures in the EDU and Daesun, though this part would be excluded in public memos.

[b]November 22-December 5, 2026: Further Negotiations, Dissolution, Continuation[/b]

The Congress of the Peoples became more divided as the month continued on, as the looming question of federalisation hung over the heads of those assembled. Among the strongest proponents were the PRA and the princes of Angmaar and Gossen, though Gossen had been quietly convinced to support federalisation by Malbern in order to stabilise the state. 

Of course Drømm, while pragmatic, knew that the federalisation of Thýven would most certainly spell out a tragic end to his vision of a united Thýven, a point he had pressed when he made the two points back in September when dealing with the communists of the city-confederation. However, recognising the divisions in the congress were merely a small window into the divisions of the entire nation, he quietly had begun to support the move of federalisation.

Thus on November 24 the congress would open the floor for discussion of the matter, while leaders of the PRA met with Drømm to secure the release of the doge under the terms that the doge swear allegiance to the central government at least on paper.  

In the meantime questions would arise around the role of the Bank of Tharkønn, which by this point had become the central bank of the nation, with Lenstahl practically holding up the economy and IDF. It was generally agreed that the collapse of the Bank of Tharkønn would be catastrophic for the Thývenic economy, thus, in meetings with the princes and the congress, Lenstahl would agree to cede the powers of the bank to the congress under a working council consisting of Lenstahl and the heads of the five regional branches. 

However, with federalisation on the table, the question now became, if the state federalised, how would the bank ensure a smooth transition under the central government. It was thus agreed that the Bank would be nationalised and formally transitioned as the new Ministry of Finance, with the external optics being that of a nationalised entity, but the internal reality being merely Lenstahl becoming a member of the transitional council, and the government having oversight over the operations of the bank. 

Debates raged on through the 26th as procedural votes stalled a final vote on federalisation, frustrating the PRA, and unnerving both the NDF and IDF. In the meantime word had spread that the Socialist Internationale had taken a mild interest in the affairs of Thýven, with a memo being sent to interested parties regarding the direction Thýven ought to take. 

On the night of the 26th Drømm and Malben met to discuss the memo, which suggested the establishment of a communist party, the halting of universal nationalisation in favour of normalisation of socialist relations, and the overall restraining of the current government into a calmer medium.  For Malben, the memo was gold, for Drømm it was further division, the old guard was still present in the country, still had a voice, and still votedin the meantime hounds cried not for centralisation but for full dissolution, both which went against the opinions of the internationale. However, Drømm wouldnt outright reject the memo, offering Malben wide permission to seek out those who were loyal to the ideas in the memo and for them to collect the necessary base to form a party, in the meantime, Drømm himself would work to establish (following the inevitable federalisation) a formal united front in the congress that could then gradually be turned red. 

Negotiations in the congress continued further, as Drømm finally agreed to release Albin Capricorn under strict oversight of the new order with Malben quietly moving to ensure Albin held no actual power upon his return to the Free Republic, quietly making a deal to install Alexandjr Ptolens (The head of the PRA) as the new head of the free republic. 

By November 28th Albin had been released under guard, a major win for the PRA thereby permitting their further cooperation in the congress, however, the monarchists and old guard, who by this point had declared the congress illegitimate, still remained a block towards the goal of "democratic" federalisation. 

Thus Drømm would quietly move to make deals with the monarchists and old guard to convince them to vote for federalisation, assuring them that whatever came next would find them comfortable among the new order, though he stopped short of promising power or authority to them. Unfortunately for Drømm his assurance fell flat with the monarchists and old guard refusing to attend the final procedural vote on November 29th, with it reporting that several moderates had already fled for Montfleur and Equestria, aware of the inevitability. 

On December 2nd the final and official vote on federalisation would be taken, with it winning the majority of the remaining congress (approximately 78 members). The congress reportedly erupted into polite applause as Drømm read off the final tally, with the congress formally being adjourned on December 3rd.

Following the vote celebrations would break out in Gossen and Knygta and Deyn as the flags of those regions were raised, in Gossen the prince would be hailed as a hero of the state, and in Knygta the PRA being treated to a ticker-tape parade in Vysjlla. 

Following December the 3rd the constitutional conventions of the principates would be formally dissolved, with a ceremonial national vote for federalisation and for the dissolution of the Holy Orthodox Empire being held across the principates on December the 5th.
